title: Length-aware dynamic batching: bucketing & padding-minimization heuristics
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: production traffic contains wide sequence-length variance which forces large padding and suboptimal kernel selection; continuous-batching by arrival time amplifies wasted compute. This PR introduces a length-aware dynamic batching heuristic with four coordinated pieces: (1) lightweight seqlen bucketing using streaming percentile estimates to avoid global sorting, (2) per-bucket padding-minimization that enforces a configurable padding budget and postpones filling under low-latency pressure, (3) adaptive merge policy that allows merging small buckets when latency SLOs permit, and (4) kernel-selection hints and scheduling tie-ins so the runtime prefers long-seq kernels when a batch majority exceeds configured thresholds. The design also adds KV-cache awareness: requests with warm caches are preferentially co-batched to reduce KV miss churn. This change exposes a runtime config key batching.seq_len_bucket_policy with options (off, conservative, aggressive) and metrics batch.padding_overhead, batch.bucket_size_distribution, batch.bucket_merge_rate. Implementation notes: bucketing uses 8 approximate buckets by default, bucket boundaries are recomputed periodically using exponentially-weighted percentile accumulators to adapt to workload shifts; padding budget is expressed as max_fraction_of_padded_tokens and defaults to 0.2; merge policy respects request-level latency budget and a new scheduling token that represents expected kernel time. Benchmarks: mixed RLHF-style workload (seqlens: 16/128/512/2048) on p4d-type nodes shows +18% throughput and -12% P95 latency for long-tail requests; cost-per-token reduced ~7% after enabling conservative policy. Rollout: feature-flagged behind batching.seq_len_bucket_policy; default remains off for Dedicated early canaries. Backwards compatibility: users can disable via config; no API break. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] implementation, [x] tests, [x] benchmarks, [x] docs and rollout plan. Related Linear items: ENG-2171, ENG-2210.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Nice approach, main concern is bucket boundary churn causing jitter — can we add a stability window?
Asha Kapoor: Added EWMA percentile window and a min_stability_period config; included tests to ensure boundaries don't flip within 10s under steady distribution.
Dana Roberts: Kernel selection hinting looks good, but we should quantify kernel switch overhead — consider a threshold to avoid thrash.
Asha Kapoor: Added a kernel-switch hysteresis and instrumentation to measure switch rate; unit added to the scheduler metrics.
Priya Nambiar: KV-cache co-batching is promising; please ensure we don't violate privacy constraints by cross-customer co-batching.
Asha Kapoor: KV-cache co-batching is scoped to tenant-id and respects isolation; added explicit checks and a dedicated unit test.
CI: flaky test test_batch_padding_budget failed on first run; rerun passed.
release_notes: Adds length-aware batching heuristics (bucketing + padding minimization) to reduce compute waste for heterogeneous sequence-length workloads. Opt-in via batching.seq_len_bucket_policy. Improves throughput on mixed-length workloads; no API changes.

~7% reduction in cost-per-token with conservative policy
